characterization: This household cooks constantly and on a tight rotation: bread, a pot of beans, potatoes, cabbage, over and over, with two or three dishes stacked on Saturday and Sunday and a single dish every other weekday. Every dish they finish has five or fewer real steps of shopping behind it — four to six ingredients. They do open the ambitious weighted-sear dishes, chicken under a brick and pressed pork belly, again and again, and back out before step one every time. Yet they cook weighted cabbage happily, which means the pressing-and-searing method isn't what they're refusing.
salientInference: Across ninety days you keep opening the brick-pressed meat dishes and cooking weighted cabbage instead — the seven-item shopping list stops you, never the technique.

signals.rhythm: Weekend stacking — two or three dishes Saturday and Sunday, one simple dish every other weekday
